cefrAlignment: B2-appropriate: the CEFR B2 written-report descriptor (synthesising and evaluating information, highlighting significant points with relevant detail) matches tasks that require selecting, grouping and comparing table and proportion data in a 150+ word report.
examFidelity: IELTS Academic Task 1 rubric wording, 150 words / 20 minutes and the overview-no-opinion requirement are accurate; pie data is presented as a table plus bar chart because the chart tool cannot draw pies, which the lesson states openly.
fixes: Model answer overview: the Total row measures time on the five listed activities, not all leisure time; reworded to 'spent the most/least time on these activities' and changed 'became more popular with age' to 'were more popular among older people' (cross-sectional data)
Model answer: '22 hours, the highest number in the table' was false (Total row has 42); now 'the highest figure for any single activity'

Model answer: 'Meeting friends was the only activity that varied little' was false (sport also varied by only 3 hours); rewritten as the only activity with no clear pattern, with accurate figures 9 → 6 → 7
Updated the walkthrough and the passage title word count (229 words) to match
ex3 gap: accepted 'highest' (growth) and '10' (one in 10) as grammatical alternatives
ex4 Q1 explanation clarified ('the share of other methods stayed the same')
Vocabulary 'the remainder' example made accurate (the remaining 40% includes 'other' methods)
openConcerns: Pie charts cannot be rendered by the chart component, so learners never practise reading an actual pie chart; a static SVG pie image would improve fidelity
learnerOutcome: A learner can pick out the key features of a table or pair of pie charts, write a figure-free overview and group the details logically with accurate proportion language.
